rationale: The mutation_baseline_run passes cleanly (exit 0, all PASS), confirming the golden is correctly graded. However, validation shows dead_check/uncovered_requirement for FR1, SR1, and SR2. Examining the actual mutants: the SR1-targeting mutant genuinely changes the root_cause narrative from a wiring/connectivity duplication defect to a fabricated logic-equation bug inside u_buf1, while keeping suspect_instances/suspect_nets identical to golden. This is a real, observable misdescription of the defect class that SR1 is supposed to catch, yet evaluate.py's SR1 check did not FAIL it -- meaning the check is not actually parsing/validating the semantic content of root_cause against the wiring-defect requirement, or is satisfied merely by the presence of the right net/instance names regardless of the accompanying narrative. Similarly, the SR2-targeting mutant swaps suspect_instances from ['u_buf1'] to ['u_voter3'] -- a genuine, unambiguous violation of SR2's requirement to name the specific cloning/buffer cell -- yet the check failed to FAIL it, indicating the SR2 check is not correctly matching on the absence of the specific instance token or is being satisfied by some other field (e.g. suspect_nets still containing correct net names) that shouldn't be sufficient on its own. FR1's dead_check status is lower severity (analyzer marks it low) but the deterministic malformed-JSON mutant should trivially trigger a FAIL if FR1's parsing check runs standalone; its non-detection suggests either a short-circuit/ordering bug or exception handling swallowing the failure silently. These are genuine evaluator discrimination gaps, not defective mutants: both the SR1 and SR2 mutants do exactly what their expected_detection describes and clearly violate the requirement semantics. mutation_score=0.714 is explicitly flagged not meaningful due to error_runs=1, and discrimination_coverage=0.625 confirms multiple real gaps. Per rules, retain_case=false and evaluation_framework must be revised.
revision_instructions: Revise evaluate.py's SR1, SR2, and FR1 checks; these are genuine discrimination gaps, not mutant defects. (1) SR1: the check must actually validate that root_cause (and/or suspect_nets) correctly characterizes the anomaly as a wiring/connectivity duplication (one replica's output net driving two voter inputs) rather than a logic-function/gate-equation defect. A mutant was introduced whose root_cause text explicitly reframes the issue as an internal logic-equation bug in the buffer cell while keeping the same instance/net name lists -- this must be FAILed. Do not grade SR1 purely by checking whether the correct net names appear somewhere in the text; parse or keyword-scan root_cause for language indicating a rewiring/duplication/aliasing defect (e.g. detect that the same source net is claimed to drive two distinct voter inputs) and FAIL if the text instead attributes the defect to an internal functional/logic bug in a cell rather than a connectivity duplication. (2) SR2: the check must FAIL when suspect_instances does not contain the specific cloning/tap instance (or an unambiguous causal description naming which replica's output feeds which voter input) and instead contains only the voter instance name. A mutant replacing suspect_instances with just the voter's own instance name was incorrectly PASSed -- tighten the check so that satisfying SR2 requires either the exact tap/buffer instance name to appear in suspect_instances, or root_cause to unambiguously name the source-replica-to-destination-voter-input relationship; naming only the voter instance without this must FAIL. (3) FR1: verify the schema-validity check is reached and correctly triggers FAIL on syntactically malformed JSON (e.g. a truncated/unparseable submission file) -- confirm no earlier check silently swallows the JSON parse exception or short-circuits in a way that returns a false PASS; add explicit exception handling around JSON parsing that maps directly to an FR1 FAIL with a clear message. Also investigate and fix the 1 mutation_execution_error (crash/timeout/unsafe path) so mutation_score becomes meaningful across all 8 requirements. All checks must grade the submitted answer's semantic content behaviorally per the pinned interface, not merely check for presence of correct net/instance name tokens irrespective of context.
